title: Public field lookup, identifiers, layout and build API
summary: Bounded field API contracts and lookup limitations.

facts.claim: For string or dot-joined array paths, with traversed keyed groups also using string or array keys, field.get(key) returns a descendant field configuration rather than an Angular control, or undefined when no descendant matches. It searches fieldGroup children in order, checks a child key for equality first, and recurses through null/undefined-key groups without consuming the requested key or through matching dotted key prefixes after consuming that prefix.
facts.context: field.get parent.get descendant fieldGroup keyless nested lookup
limits: The search starts below the field on which get is called; it does not search parents or siblings automatically.

Scalar numeric-key traversal is not guaranteed: a numeric lookup request can throw when traversal reaches key.indexOf for a keyed child group. The undefined-on-miss statement is limited to the string/dot-joined-array paths described above.
facts.source_quote: For string or dot-joined array paths, with traversed keyed groups also using string or array keys, field.get(key) returns a descendant field configuration rather than an Angular control, or undefined when no descendant matches. It searches fieldGroup children in order, checks a child key for equality first, and recurses through null/undefined-key groups without consuming the requested key or through matching dotted key prefixes after consuming that prefix. [K05](sources.md#k05) [K140](sources.md#k140)

facts.claim: field.get joins array keys with dots for both the request and child keys. Consequently ["a.b"] and ["a", "b"] are indistinguishable to this lookup. Unlike getKeyPath, this lookup does not normalize bracket notation.
facts.context: field.get array key dot bracket control lookup path limits
limits: This field-tree lookup is not interchangeable with Angular control lookup or a guarantee that every accepted field key shape is traversed identically. A key on a field configuration and a control in a parent form are different lookup targets.
facts.source_quote: field.get joins array keys with dots for both the request and child keys. Consequently ["a.b"] and ["a", "b"] are indistinguishable to this lookup. Unlike getKeyPath, this lookup does not normalize bracket notation. [K140](sources.md#k140) [K39](sources.md#k39)

facts.claim: key links a field value to the model; id specifies its field HTML identifier and is generated when not supplied; name is a separately configurable field name. formlyAttributes sets a truthy field.name on its DOM element and, for its single attached element when no directive id input is supplied, applies field.id.
facts.context: key id name model DOM identifier formlyAttributes generated id
limits: Setting name or id does not replace key as the model path. These DOM effects require a template using formlyAttributes; multiple attached elements and an explicit directive id input have separate handling.
facts.source_quote: key links a field value to the model; id specifies its field HTML identifier and is generated when not supplied; name is a separately configurable field name. formlyAttributes sets a truthy field.name on its DOM element and, for its single attached element when no directive id input is supplied, applies field.id. [K01](sources.md#k01) [K05](sources.md#k05) [K37](sources.md#k37)

facts.claim: className targets the outer formly-field component. fieldGroupClassName targets the built-in formly-group component, whose host class binding uses field.fieldGroupClassName or an empty string.
facts.context: className fieldGroupClassName CSS layout outer formly-field formly-group host
limits: These properties do not automatically style an inner Material input or wrapper. A custom group template must implement its own class bindings if it needs this behavior.
facts.source_quote: className targets the outer formly-field component. fieldGroupClassName targets the built-in formly-group component, whose host class binding uses field.fieldGroupClassName or an empty string. [K01](sources.md#k01) [K41](sources.md#k41) [K141](sources.md#k141)

facts.claim: The public FieldArrayTypeConfig<T> interface extends FormlyFieldConfig<T>, requires formControl: FormArray and props: NonNullable<T>, and is the default generic configuration for FieldArrayType.
facts.context: FieldArrayTypeConfig FieldArrayType typed FormArray props generic
limits: This is the array control typing contract; FieldTypeConfig and FieldGroupTypeConfig have their separately covered scalar and group control shapes. It is not a general compile-time proof that an arbitrary runtime field has the expected control.
facts.source_quote: The public FieldArrayTypeConfig<T> interface extends FormlyFieldConfig<T>, requires formControl: FormArray and props: NonNullable<T>, and is the default generic configuration for FieldArrayType. [K02](sources.md#k02) [K142](sources.md#k142)

facts.claim: FormlyFormOptions declares build(field?) returning FormlyFieldConfig. When root builder setup finds no existing options.build, it installs a callback that builds its supplied field, defaults to that root field when omitted, and returns the field that it built.
facts.context: options.build rebuild root supplied field optional callback return
limits: This describes the builder-installed default; a caller-supplied options.build is preserved. Rebuilding is distinct from the separately covered checkExpressions and detectChanges operations; it is not a promise to recreate every control or preserve ad-hoc control validators.

When root builder setup finds no existing options.build, it installs a callback that builds its supplied field, defaults to that root field when omitted, and returns the field that it built.
